Hi Samir — thanks again for the detailed demo earlier. Quick recap and the handful of items we promised to follow up on related to authentication and key management so your security team can review: 

1) Recommended auth model: we suggested two supported options depending on your risk tolerance — long-lived API keys scoped to a single project + rotation schedule (simpler for batch jobs) OR short-lived JWT-backed tokens minted by your identity provider (OIDC) with Azure AD / Okta recommended for SSO flows.

2) Service accounts & delegation: for server-to-server we recommend one service account per environment (prod/stage) with least-privilege roles in Redwood Private. We also proposed using signed JWTs for shorter-lived credentials when calling the hosted API.

3) Key rotation and KMS: you asked about rotation automation — we propose integrating your KMS (Azure Key Vault) with our rotation webhook so keys are rolled monthly and old tokens are automatically invalidated. Draft rotation policy attached.

4) SDK setup & routing: we will provide SDK examples that wire the token source (env var, local KMS cache, or OIDC token exchange) into the client wrapper. Routing: traffic can be pinned to our Dedicated pool for FinLytics prod; SDK will accept a route hint header.

Action items / proposed timeline:
- I’ll share a short design diagram and a draft rotation policy for your security review (attached).
- Security to confirm whether they prefer API keys or OIDC as the primary pattern by Wed 8/25.
- If OIDC preferred, Priyom will share a sample token exchange flow and the SDK snippet by Monday 8/24.

Would you be able to loop in your security lead on the reply? If easier, we can set a 30-min follow-up to finalize the pattern.

Thanks — quick technical summary and recommended deliverables we can hand to FinLytics security: 

- Recommended default: OIDC-issued short-lived JWTs (1–15 min TTL) minted by FinLytics IdP. Redwood validates via standard JWKS endpoint (RS256). For clients that cannot perform OIDC exchange, we support our own short-lived service tokens (signed by Redwood, 1 hour TTL) with automated revocation lists.

- Batch jobs: allow a scoped API key with strict IP allowlist + 7-day rotation. Integrate with Azure Key Vault via the Azure Key Vault SDK: we can poll KV for the current key or accept webhook notifications on rotate. Our rotation handler includes retry/backoff (exponential backoff with jitter) and a grace window where both old/new keys are accepted for up to 5 minutes to avoid in-flight failures.

- Service accounts: we should recommend a per-environment service account and minimum set of scopes (ingest-only vs read-only embeddings). We will provide Terraform snippets for creating service principals and roles in the customer's IAM.

- SDK patterns to ship with the example:
  * TokenProvider interface: env var | local KMS fetch | OIDC exchange.
  * Automatic refresh: background refresh thread that pre-fetches tokens 20% before expiry; fallback to synchronous exchange on 401.
  * Retry semantics: idempotent token-refresh + request retry with backoff; avoid retrying non-idempotent calls by default.
  * Routing hint: header X-Redwood-Route: dedicated-prod-finlytics (sample in SDK).

Deliverables I’ll produce by EOD:
- Short design diagram (PNG) with auth flows (attached).
- SDK token-exchange snippet (Node + Python) and a sample Terraform role binding.
- Draft rotation webhook spec (URL, payload, retries) — we will include webhook signing (HMAC) so FinLytics can validate events.

If Azra wants to review the JWT claims we assert on the service tokens, point them to the JWKS endpoint we’ll provide (https://api.redwood.ai/.well-known/jwks.json) and the token claim validator spec.

Happy to jump on a 20-min call with FinLytics security to go through the flow.
